postgresql.title: PostgreSQL
postgresql.summary: PostgreSQL is an open-source object-relational database known for strict ACID compliance, a mature SQL feature set, and deep extensibility.
key_points: Strict ACID transactions with MVCC concurrency control
Rich support for JSONB, full-text search, and extensions such as PostGIS
Vertical scaling is strong; horizontal write-scaling needs extensions like Citus
Best suited for workloads needing complex joins, strong consistency, and relational integrity

mongodb.title: MongoDB
mongodb.summary: MongoDB is a document-oriented NoSQL database that stores data as flexible, JSON-like BSON documents.
key_points: Schema-flexible document model well suited to evolving or nested data
Native horizontal scaling via sharding
Tunable consistency: eventual by default, strong with majority write/read concern
Best suited for high write-throughput, denormalized, rapidly-iterating workloads

redis.title: Redis
redis.summary: Redis is an in-memory key-value store used for caching, session storage, queues, and real-time leaderboards.
key_points: Sub-millisecond reads and writes from an in-memory data model
Rich data structures: strings, hashes, sorted sets, streams, HyperLogLog
Optional persistence via RDB snapshots and an append-only file
Not a primary system of record for large datasets that exceed available memory

kafka.title: Apache Kafka
kafka.summary: Kafka is a distributed event-streaming platform built around durable, partitioned, append-only logs.
key_points: High-throughput, ordered-per-partition log with configurable retention
Decouples producers and consumers; supports replay and multiple independent consumer groups
Scales horizontally by adding brokers and partitions
Operationally heavier than a simple message queue; shines at sustained high volume

kubernetes.title: Kubernetes
kubernetes.summary: Kubernetes is a container-orchestration system that automates deployment, scaling, and recovery of containerized workloads.
key_points: Declarative desired-state model reconciled by control-loop controllers
Built-in self-healing, rolling updates, and horizontal pod autoscaling
Service discovery and load balancing via a built-in DNS and virtual IPs
Steep operational learning curve relative to simpler PaaS options

docker.title: Docker
docker.summary: Docker packages applications and their dependencies into portable, isolated containers sharing the host kernel.
key_points: Images are layered and cacheable, giving fast, reproducible builds
Containers start in milliseconds, far faster than a full virtual machine
A single Docker host has no built-in multi-node scheduling (that is what Kubernetes adds)
The de facto standard container image format and runtime interface

graphql.title: GraphQL
graphql.summary: GraphQL is a query language and runtime for APIs that lets clients request exactly the fields they need.
key_points: Clients avoid both over-fetching and under-fetching with a single typed endpoint
A strongly typed schema serves as executable API documentation
Caching is harder than plain REST because requests are not simple URLs
Well suited to aggregating many backend sources behind one graph

rest api.title: REST API
rest api.summary: REST is an architectural style for networked APIs built around stateless requests to named resources over HTTP.
key_points: Resources are addressed by URL and manipulated with standard HTTP verbs
Simple to cache, load-balance, and reason about at the HTTP layer
Can require multiple round trips for deeply nested or related data
The most widely adopted API style across the industry

python.title: Python
python.summary: Python is a dynamically typed, interpreted language prized for readability and an enormous ecosystem.
key_points: Readable syntax and a 'batteries included' standard library speed up development
Dominant ecosystem for data science, ML, and scripting
The GIL limits true multi-threaded CPU parallelism within one process
Slower raw execution than compiled languages for CPU-bound inner loops

rust.title: Rust
rust.summary: Rust is a compiled systems language that guarantees memory safety without a garbage collector via its ownership model.
key_points: Ownership and borrow-checking eliminate whole classes of memory bugs at compile time
Performance comparable to C/C++ with no garbage-collection pauses
Steeper learning curve due to the borrow checker
Growing adoption in performance- and safety-critical infrastructure

transformer architecture.title: Transformer architecture
transformer architecture.summary: The transformer is a neural network architecture built on self-attention, enabling parallel processing of sequences.
key_points: Self-attention lets every token weigh every other token directly, without recurrence
Parallelizable training made today's large-scale language models practical
Attention cost grows quadratically with sequence length
The foundation of modern large language models

reinforcement learning.title: Reinforcement learning
reinforcement learning.summary: Reinforcement learning trains an agent to choose actions that maximize cumulative reward through trial-and-error interaction with an environment.
key_points: Learns from reward signals rather than labeled examples
Well suited to sequential decision problems: games, robotics, control
Often sample-inefficient; can need millions of environment interactions
Reward design mistakes can lead to unintended, exploitative behavior

microservices.title: Microservices
microservices.summary: Microservices structure an application as a set of small, independently deployable services communicating over the network.
key_points: Independent deployment and scaling per service, by independent teams
Failure isolation keeps one service's outage from taking down the whole system
Adds distributed-systems complexity: network calls, partial failure, versioning
Needs real operational investment in observability and service discovery

serverless.title: Serverless computing
serverless.summary: Serverless computing runs short-lived functions on infrastructure that is fully managed and scaled by the provider.
key_points: No servers to provision or patch; the platform scales to zero and back up
Billing is typically per invocation and execution time
Cold starts can add latency to infrequently invoked functions
Long-running or stateful workloads are a poor fit
